summary: Polk County, OR platform on three trees, built 1929 by a fire patrol association and staffed into 1942; removed or destroyed in 1959. No source describes the peak today.

facts.design: Platform on three Douglas fir trees, guyed with steel cables, with a stairway and a small cabin on top
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1959; no source describes what remains on the peak today
facts.agency: Lincoln FPA (per register); the 1929 builder was the Polk County fire patrol association

events.note: Built in spring 1929 per register and a June 1929 newspaper item
Mrs. Sawtell (spelled two ways) had charge of the lookout in 1931
Fire warden reported snow damage to the house, March 1937
June 1942 inspection report: married couple Mr. and Mrs. Walter Isbell occupied the station
Register says removed in 1959; Forest Lookouts lists 1959 as Removed
firelookout.com says destroyed in 1959; a 1960 survey note says the local fire marshal reported the station destroyed
Registered November 8, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says three 90-foot trees; firelookout.com says three 50-foot trees; the 1929 item says the trees were topped at 90 feet; a 1941 survey note says the finished tower was about 80 feet (24.4 m, the height_m fact). Not resolved; the story reports each.

All three agree on 1959. The register says removed, firelookout.com says destroyed, and a 1960 survey note records a report of destruction by the local fire marshal. The manner of its end is not resolved.

The register says administered by Lincoln FPA; the 1929 item credits the Polk county fire patrol association; the Forest Lookouts page heads its entries Lincoln County Fire Patrol. The sources do not explain the change in name.
Two 1931 papers spell the lookout's name Sawtell and Sawtelle, and one gives a first name. The story does not pick one spelling.

notes_for_editor: Source [3] reproduces a 1941 USC&GS / 1960 DMA survey description for the Dorn Peak station (designation DORN PEAK LOT, PID QE2307). The survey mark and bronze disks may still exist; that was not checked on the NGS datasheet, so the story says no source describes the peak today. Access: sources give no current access information; the 1941 survey route through a gate is old and was left out. Record height_m 24.4 is supported by the 80-foot NGS figure. Register elevation 868 m matches the record. Dorn vs Doran spelling appears in the 1929 item.
